title: Design warm baseline build to cut checks-stage time
summary: Write a design note under docs/design/ for a warm baseline build of main (keyed by hash of rust-toolchain.toml and Cargo.lock, refreshed in the background) so checks stop starting from an empty target dir. It cites review 20261029-155931-wfkr, states the 8.0-minute predicted saving and how the next review measures it. rust-toolchain.toml is not changed.

defaults_applied.how: Note cites THROUGHPUT.md figures and labels estimates.
Note states how the next review measures the saving.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: a design note for the warm-baseline build change; audience is Athena's maintainer and the next throughput review, which scores the predicted saving.
The job is docs-only: it designs the change but does not implement it; implementation would be a later job citing review 20261029-155931-wfkr.
rust-toolchain.toml is named in the request only as an input to the cache key; this job does not change it.
Existing code: docs/ design documents and THROUGHPUT.md are read for context; the note is new and creates no code.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new design note exists under docs/design/ (e.g. docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md) that describes the warm baseline build of main keyed by a hash of rust-toolchain.toml and Cargo.lock, its background refresh, and how checks (fmt, clippy, test) start from it instead of an empty CARGO_TARGET_DIR; checkable by reading the file.

The note cites throughput review 20261029-155931-wfkr and the measured figures from THROUGHPUT.md (14.1 of 25.4 minutes median per landed job in checks; producer 6.8), labeling any other number as an estimate.

The note states the predicted saving of 8.0 minutes per landed job and names how the next throughput review measures it (the median minutes per landed job over the last 20, with checks-stage minutes compared against 14.1 and 25.4).
The note lists alternatives considered (e.g. shared target dir, sccache, no change) and risks such as stale cache and correctness of verification from a warm build, and reviews them.
rust-toolchain.toml is only read and cited as the cache key input; git diff shows no change to it, nor to athena.toml, defaults.toml, Cargo.lock or any file outside docs/design/.

out_of_scope: rust-toolchain.toml (read as a cache key input only; must not change)
Implementing the warm baseline build in crates/ or xtask/
